prompts.data.formula.detailed: Explain this [Excel or Google Sheets] formula: [formula]. Break it into parts: what each function does, which cells it refers to, what the result will be. Give an example with made-up numbers. Say when the formula would return an error.
prompts.data.formula.refine: Can this formula be written more simply? Show an alternative and explain the difference.
prompts.data.formula.check: Here's how I understand the formula: [explanation]. Is that right?
prompts.data.structure.short: What columns does a spreadsheet for [task] need?
prompts.data.structure.detailed: Help me design a spreadsheet for [task]. What I'll need to find out from it: [questions]. Suggest columns: name, data type (text, number, date, list), example value, required or not. One row per record. Don't add columns for personal data if they're not needed.
prompts.data.structure.refine: Which columns should be drop-down lists to avoid typos?
prompts.data.structure.check: Here are my columns: [columns]. Will I be able to answer [question]?
prompts.data.write.short: Write a formula for [Excel or Google Sheets]: [what to calculate]
prompts.data.write.detailed: I need a formula for [Excel or Google Sheets]. Data: [where things are, e.g. “column A has dates, B has amounts”]. Goal: [what to calculate]. Give the formula, explain it step by step, say what happens with empty cells, and suggest how to handle errors. Function language: [Russian or English].
prompts.data.write.refine: The formula returns [error]. What could be causing it?
prompts.data.write.check: Give me 5 test rows with expected results so I can check the formula.
prompts.data.error.short: Why is my spreadsheet total wrong: [description]?
prompts.data.error.detailed: The total is [result] but should be about [expected]. Formula: [formula]. The data looks like: [sample rows, no personal data]. List possible causes by likelihood: numbers stored as text, extra spaces, hidden rows, wrong range, absolute vs relative references. For each, how to check.
prompts.data.error.refine: It's [cause]. How do I fix it for the whole column at once?
prompts.data.error.check: How can I set up the sheet so this doesn't happen again?
prompts.data.clean.short: How should I clean this data: [problems]?
prompts.data.clean.detailed: I need to tidy up some data. Sample rows (no personal data): [sample]. Problems: [problems]. Suggest an order of steps: duplicates, spaces, letter case, date and number formats, typos in categories, empty values. For each, how to do it in [Excel or Google Sheets] and how to check the result.
prompts.data.clean.refine: How can I set this up once so the cleaning repeats automatically for new data?
prompts.data.clean.check: After cleaning I have [number] rows out of [before]. Is that plausible? What should I check?
prompts.data.group.short: How do I group the data by [field] and calculate [what]?
prompts.data.group.detailed: Data: [which columns]. I need to group by [field] and calculate [what] for each group. Explain 2 ways in [Excel or Google Sheets]: a pivot table and formulas. For each, step by step, pros and cons, and what to do when the data updates.
prompts.data.group.refine: Add grouping by month, since the data has a date.
prompts.data.group.check: Which conclusions does this grouping support, and which would be a stretch?
prompts.data.questions.short: What questions could this data answer? [columns]
prompts.data.questions.detailed: I have a table with columns: [columns], about [number] rows, covering [period]. Suggest 10 analysis questions, from simple (how many, what's the average) to comparisons and trends. For each, what calculation or chart is needed and the limits of the answer.
prompts.data.questions.refine: What data would I need to add to answer [question]?
prompts.data.questions.check: My conclusion: [conclusion]. Am I confusing correlation with causation?
prompts.data.chart.short: Explain what this chart shows: [chart description]
prompts.data.chart.detailed: Here's a chart: type [type], X axis [what], Y axis [what], values: [values]. Explain: the main finding in one sentence, notable changes, outliers, what the chart doesn't show. Say whether this chart type suits the data or another would be better.
prompts.data.chart.refine: Suggest a chart title that states the finding right away.
prompts.data.chart.check: My caption for the chart: [text]. Am I claiming more than the chart shows?
prompts.data.check.short: How can I check the spreadsheet calculation is right: [what was calculated]?
prompts.data.check.detailed: I calculated in a spreadsheet: [what was calculated], and got [result]. Suggest 5 ways to check it: an order-of-magnitude estimate, recalculating another way, checking a small sample by hand, reconciling totals, looking for outliers. For each, exactly what to do.
prompts.data.check.refine: Check [method] gave a different result: [result]. Where should I look for the discrepancy?
prompts.data.check.check: Which checks should I run every time I update this sheet?
prompts.data.missing.short: What should I do about missing values in [column]?
prompts.data.missing.detailed: There are gaps in the data: column [column], about [percent]% of rows. The data is about [subject]. List the options: drop rows, leave blank, fill with mean or median, carry the previous value forward, flag separately. For each, when it fits and how it would bias the conclusions.
prompts.data.missing.refine: Why might the values be missing? Which causes are worth checking?
prompts.data.missing.check: I chose [method]. How do I report that honestly?

verify.data.formula: Test the formula on 2–3 rows where you can work out the answer by hand.
verify.data.structure: Before filling hundreds of rows, try the structure with 10 records.
verify.data.write: Test the formula on a copy of the sheet and on edge cases: empty cells, zeros, text instead of numbers.
verify.data.error: Look for the error on a copy of the file so you don't damage the data by accident.
verify.data.clean: Save the original before cleaning. Spot-check every batch of deleted rows.
verify.data.group: Check that group totals add up to the overall total: if not, some data got lost.
verify.data.questions: Data only answers the questions it was collected for. Don't draw conclusions about what isn't in it.
verify.data.chart: Look at the axes: does the scale start at zero, is the step even? A truncated axis exaggerates differences.
verify.data.check: The most reliable check is to recalculate the key figure a different way.
verify.data.missing: Filling gaps changes the data. Mark which values are filled in rather than measured.
